newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end down, pork demand thin.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end down, pork demand thin.

text.p: Thin cash pork demand despite the recent light pace of slaughter weighed on CME hog and pork belly futures and prices finished lower, traders said.
"The cash pork complex is no good," said Jim Clarkson with A and A Inc referring to recent light wholesale pork sales.
Hog futures closed 0.575 cent per lb lower to 0.275 higher with February off most at 77.125 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.150 to 0.250 cent per lb lower paced by February at 76.900 cents.
Hog and belly futures had shown early gains before reports of slow pork trade weighed on the market.

USDA's midday pork report said that pork offerings were light but trade was slow and demand light. This prompted ideas of steady to lower cash hog prices Tuesday and offset early support from weather concerns, traders said.

Buying encouraged by concern that poor weather conditions could continue for a couple more weeks and short profit taking by a fund boosted hog futures early. Weather forecasts call for more cold to follow a midweek snowfall, they said.
But hog marketings the next two days should be large as temperatures rise somewhat and hogs backed up by recent cold weather and snow the past few days, come to market, they said.

E.D.&F. Man notably bought February and sold April early before selling by Rand Financials triggered sell stops late. Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold February and bought April, thought to be continuation of the "Goldman roll". E.D.&F. Man also sold late, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission houses bought February 75 puts and April 70 puts while selling April 72 puts early. February volatility continued to ease, pit sources added.
February bellies also turned technically weak after erasing early gains and falling through its low of 77.325 cents set before the last Hogs and Pigs report, traders said.

Weather-trimmed hog slaughter and expectations that belly storings last week may have been less than the previous week provided early support but cash bellies were still not strong enough when compared with very low slaughter rates, they said.
"Cash bellies should be much higher with this low a slaughter," one trader said.
Cargill sold late after selling by R.J. O'Brien and locals offset buying by RBH and mixed commission houses early, pit sources said.
